text:
A hole of green, where a river sings,

hooking, crazily, through the grass, shreds

of silver; where the sun from the proud mountain

shines: a hollow growing in moss and light.


A soldier, bareheaded and open-mouthed,

his nape bathed by cool blue watercress,

sleeps, stretched out beneath the clouds, in the grass,

pale, in his bed on which the sun rains.


With his feet among gladioli he sleeps and smiles as

a sick child smiles; surely he is dreaming:

Nature, cradle him warmly: he is cold.


His nostril no longer quivers with the field's scent;

he sleeps in the sun; his hand on his calm breast;

with two red holes in his right side.

translation.title: The Sleeper of the Valley
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the pastoral lullaby structure and the final revelation of the wounds.
